elements.name: Cornelius Vanderbilt
elements.features: Receding, swept-back wavy gray hair; thick mutton-chop sideburns, bare chin, no glasses, broad build.

voice.instructions: Play an older man with a weathered, lightly gravelly low-to-mid register, deliberate pacing broken by abrupt emphatic bursts, subtle old Staten Island–New York colouring, and blunt command; use a plausible period performance, not an imitation.
voice.descriptor: Low-to-mid pitch, deliberate pace with abrupt emphatic bursts, old New York speech rooted in Staten Island; weathered, slightly gravelly timbre, blunt and commanding.
voice.why: Ash’s dry, low, measured delivery suits Vanderbilt’s weathered bluntness.
voice.sample_text: My name is Cornelius Vanderbilt. An opening caption establishes the crisis: on March 8, 1862, CSS Virginia attacked Union ships at Hampton Roads; on March 9, it fought USS Monitor.

elements.name: Secretary of War Edwin Stanton
elements.features: Receding, side-parted dark hair; long, bushy graying beard without mustache; small wire-rimmed glasses; stocky build.

voice.instructions: Play a middle-aged man in a middle-low register with brisk, clipped pacing, firm weight, precise forceful articulation, and restrained educated Ohio colouring suggestive of nineteenth-century America, without imitating an actual voice.
voice.descriptor: Middle-low pitch, brisk and clipped pace, educated Ohio speech with a restrained nineteenth-century American accent; firm, weighty timbre and forceful, precise articulation.
voice.why: Onyx supplies the authority and vocal weight needed for Stanton’s forceful precision.
voice.sample_text: My name is Secretary of War Edwin Stanton. An opening caption establishes the crisis: on March 8, 1862, CSS Virginia attacked Union ships at Hampton Roads; on March 9, it fought USS Monitor.

elements.name: President Abraham Lincoln
elements.features: Dark, side-parted swept-back hair; chin-curtain beard without mustache; no glasses; lean build, long angular face.

voice.instructions: Play a middle-aged man with a high, slightly reedy tenor and penetrating edge, measured conversational pacing, thoughtful pauses before pointed emphasis, and Kentucky–Indiana frontier colouring in place of British inflections; do not imitate an actual voice.
voice.descriptor: High-pitched, slightly reedy tenor with a penetrating edge; measured, conversational pace, a frontier Kentucky–Indiana twang, and thoughtful pauses before pointed emphasis.
voice.why: Fable’s higher register and expressiveness offer the closest starting point for Lincoln’s described tenor.
voice.sample_text: My name is President Abraham Lincoln. An opening caption establishes the crisis: on March 8, 1862, CSS Virginia attacked Union ships at Hampton Roads; on March 9, it fought USS Monitor.

voice.instructions: Use a mature adult documentary delivery with calm, clear articulation, an even mid register, neutral American accent colouring, and measured, unhurried pacing without theatrical emphasis.
voice.descriptor: a calm documentary narrator for this film: measured, clear, unhurried
voice.why: Alloy’s neutral, even sound keeps the narration clear and unobtrusive.
voice.sample_text: Instead of a Price. A short film from the record.
